einzeiler: Mary Carillo and Pam Shriver live from the U.S. Open discussing tennis and life.
kurzfassung: Mary Carillo reflects on her upcoming Hall of Fame induction, growing up alongside John McEnroe, and transitioning from player to broadcaster due to knee injuries. Pam Shriver shares stories from her historic 1978 U.S. Open run at age 16, her legendary doubles partnership with Martina Navratilova, and her current coaching work. Both legends discuss the mindset, resilience, and enduring joy that tennis has brought them throughout their lives.
stichpunkte: Mary Carillo discusses her upcoming induction into the International Tennis Hall of Fame alongside Roger Federer.
Carillo recalls growing up in Queens with John McEnroe and winning the 1977 French Open mixed doubles title with him.
Severe knee injuries forced Carillo to end her playing career, leading her into a successful broadcasting career starting with the USA Network.
Carillo reflects on covering 17 Olympic Games, including stepping in at the last minute to host the Milan opening ceremony.
Pam Shriver talks about reaching the 1978 U.S. Open singles final at just 16 years old after defeating Martina Navratilova.
Shriver details her highly successful doubles partnership with Navratilova, earning 20 Grand Slam titles together.
Both guests discuss their current work as coaches, focusing heavily on mental toughness, mindset management, and breathing techniques.
The conversation touches on personal resilience, including navigating family life and raising children with type 1 diabetes.

clips.hook: How Mary Carillo found out about her Hall of Fame induction
clips.text: The requirements for entering the International Tennis Hall of Fame as a contributor differ from player rules, and finding out about the honor came via a surprising Zoom call.

clips.hook: Knowing your limits and celebrating a tournament win
clips.text: Growing up alongside elite talent showed the speaker her own performance ceiling, which ultimately fostered a deep appreciation for the game and made winning a smaller tournament feel uniquely satisfying.

clips.hook: Being the youngest U.S. Open finalist at age 16
clips.text: Reaching a major final as a teenager happened during a very different era of the sport when depth was lower, making records set back then stand out distinctively.

clips.hook: An unexpected phone call from Martina Navratilova
clips.text: A casual phone call received via a tournament director before cell phones existed opened the door to a partnership that served as a direct ticket to the Hall of Fame.

clips.hook: The heavy mental pressure of professional tennis
clips.text: Elite athletes face immense distractions regarding rankings and massive prize money during high-stakes moments, making emotional control a difficult but essential skill.

beschreibung:
Hoda takes Joy 101 to the U.S. Open with tennis legends Mary Carillo and Pam Shriver.
"The hardest thing in the world is doing something you've never done before, but... it's fun to say yes to things." -Mary Carillo
"Chrissy beat me 18 straight times out of the gate before I got her. And then Martina, while I got her early, she beat me 33 straight times at the end of our career. But tennis brings you together." -Pam Shriver
